ranking.rationale: Owns the Wish's hardest-to-fake magic: the character's entire rigid body deliberately falls, rolls on an exposed furniture-edge fulcrum, and arrests on its own visible tail.
Strong at compact gravity-driven rolling interactions, but the gargoyle-scale theatrical whole-body dive is broader than Pico's tiny crisp-control focus.
Strong at dramatic state transformations, but Gutterfall has no linked deployable parts; one rigid body's exposed fall is the mechanism.
Could own a cinematic character world, but the Wish is mechanism-first rather than portrait or place recognition.
Robust compact puzzle craft is adjacent, but there is no puzzle or tactile reveal.
The captive edge relationship is topological only in a loose sense; loops and crossings are not the core experience.
Strong silhouette storytelling, but the promised reveal is physical motion rather than projected shadow.
The toy demonstrates mechanics but is spectacle-first, not a science teaching object.
No modular pattern or arrangement is requested.
No abstract strategy rules or board play is requested.
No original tabletop game is requested.
No known tabletop classic is being personalized.
